newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM to dissolve parliament on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM to dissolve parliament on Friday.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told his partners in Japan's coalition government on Thursday that he will dissolve the Lower House of parliament on Friday.

Sakigake president Shoichi Ide disclosed the prime minister's comment to reporters after a meeting of the three coalition party leaders. General elections must be called within 40 days of a dissolution of parliament.

The timing of the dissolution and general elections had been widely leaked to the domestic media by politicians. Coalition politicians had said elections would held on October 20 if parliament was dissolved on Friday.
"The prime minister told us there was no other time when parliament could be dissolved than at the opening of its special session on Friday," Ide told reporters.
He said it was up to the prime minister when to dissolve parliament and call general elections.

Polls are not mandated until July 1997, but Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party favours going before voters as early as possible before April, when a rise in the unpopular consumption tax, approved by his government, takes effect. The tax is to be raised to five percent from three percent.
